title: Debt-managed burst ledger and tenant retreat playbook (PRD draft)
content:
Context:

This is a working PRD for a cadenceable playbook that combines a per-tenant burst "ledger" (a bounded credit accounting system), an operational ‘tenant retreat’ (soft-suspension + controlled unwind) flow, and autoscale steering signals. Goal is to allow safe, transient overcommit in Dedicated pools while keeping unit economics predictable and minimizing eviction shock to customers.

Why this matters (problem statement):
- Customers want burst headroom beyond reserved capacity (seasonal campaigns, launches). Dedicated pools can’t be infinite and noisy neighbors reduce SLOs.
- Current burst approaches either: a) aggressively prewarm extra capacity (costly), or b) indiscriminately throttle (bad UX), or c) evict with blunt force (surprising and high customer toil).
- We need a middle ground that: preserves latency SLOs, recovers cost via debt accounting, and offers clear, predictable behavior that customers can program against.

High-level product goals (success metrics):
- Allow up to X% transient oversubscription per pool while keeping p95 latency regressed < 10% vs baseline.
- Limit unexpected hard-evictions to < 0.5% of tenants per month during burst events.
- Recover > 70% of incremental cost from burst via billing credits/debit reconciliation where applicable.
- Enable customers to opt-in or configure retreat sensitivity and debt tolerance in Console.

User personas & key user stories:
- Platform engineer (internal): needs predictable, instrumentable rules to debug and tune pool behavior during peak days.
- Tenant SRE/Product: wants clear SLAs during bursts, ability to define opt-in fidelity lanes and debt budget.
- Billing/Finance: needs auditable ledger records for burst consumption to enable invoices/credits.

Example user stories:
- As a tenant owner, I want 5x short-term burst headroom for Sale Day, but only if I accept a repayable credit charge and softer tail-latency guarantees.
- As an operator, I want a deterministic retreat plan that gracefully drains KV caches and reissues token rejections to callers at controlled rates.
- As billing, I need per-tenant burst ledger entries with timestamps, cost basis, and manual adjustment audit trail.

Design overview (components):
1) Burst Ledger (per-tenant credit model)
- Each tenant has a numeric credit balance representing pre-authorized burst capacity. Credits are earned (reserved or purchased) and debited as burst compute is used beyond baseline reserved lanes.
- Ledger entry: id, tenant_id, timestamp, delta_credits, reason_tag, cost_estimate, operator_note (audit); stored in an append-only ledger with retention policy.
- Credit semantics: can be positive (pre-purchased), zero (no burst), or negative within a configurable tolerance window (debt). Debt has TTL and an amortization schedule.

2) Debt-managed burst policy semantics
- Soft debt cap: per-tenant negative credit limit (configurable per plan). While within cap, traffic flows and tenant rides a degraded fidelity lane (e.g., lower concurrency, batched inference, quantized model variant).
- Debt TTL: if debt remains unpaid past TTL, tenant enters Retreat flow (soft-suspension). TTL defaults: 72 hours for standard plans, customizable for enterprise.
- Repayment paths: automatic reconciliation via billing (invoice offset), manual top-up via Console, or automatic throttled reductions in throughput to reduce ongoing debt accrual.

3) Tenant Retreat flow (controlled unwind)
- Trigger conditions: debt > cap OR pool headroom falls below critical threshold AND tenant in high-debt state.
- Retreat phases:
  - Phase 0 (notice): enqueue an informational event to tenant (console, webhooks) plus a transient API header X-Redwood-Burst-Warning.
  - Phase 1 (soft-contain): shift tenant to a fidelity lane (quantized model or lower batch priority), reduce concurrency limit incrementally (configurable step-down). Prefetches and warm caches preserved for N minutes.
  - Phase 2 (drain): stop new long-lived sessions, allow in-flight inference to finish, drain KV cache TTL aggressively, emit final ledger snapshot.
  - Phase 3 (soft-suspend): return 429/503 for new requests according to ramp schedule with Retry-After guidance and structured error body that includes debt balance and pay-up link.
- Automated rollback: if headroom recovers or tenant tops-up credits, unroll phases in reverse with hysteresis.

4) Autoscaler integration and steering signals
- Autoscaler consumes pool-level signals and tenant-level priority (computed from credits, recent p95 delta, and explicit customer tier).
- During pool pressure, autoscaler will: pause opportunistic warm-pool expansion for low-credit tenants, prioritize warm-starts for high-credit/enterprise tenants, and orchestrate preemptive retirements for opportunistic nodes.
- Feedback loop: ledger debits are emitted as a metric stream (redwood.burst.ledger.delta) so autoscaler ML models can learn tenant burst patterns and avoid oscillation.

Operational & Console UX
- Console: per-tenant burst dashboard (current balance, recent deltas, estimated cost-to-date, TTL clock, historical events). Controls: top-up, set debt tolerance, set auto-pay, opt-in fidelity lanes, view retreat timeline test.
- Admin runbook: clear steps for manual intervention (force-topup, force-drain, emergency isolation, manual invoice adjustment). Playbook includes safe fallbacks to hosted API for critical tenants.

Billing model notes
- Default: burst is free up to a soft cap, negative balance accrues and appears on next invoice as a repayable charge. For enterprise customers, we expose a pre-agreed grace band with longer TTL and negotiated cost per unit.
- Cost attribution: cost_estimate per ledger delta uses model cost profile (tokens/sec * model_unit_cost + infra amortized). There will be a variance allowance bucket for noisy measurements.

Telemetry & SLOs to monitor
- Metrics: per-tenant credit_balance, credit_delta_rate, debt_ttl_remaining, retreat_phase, p50/p95/p99 latency by tenant and by lane, pool_headroom_ratio, ledger_write_latency, billing_mismatch_rate.
- Alerts: burst debt drift > X over 24h, retreat_count > baseline, spike in hard evictions.

Safety checks & guardrails
- No single tenant can push pool headroom usage > Y% without a signed enterprise override.
- Isolation fence: when a tenant crosses a high-risk threshold, that tenant’s requests are logically isolated into a sandbox queue so other tenants see minimal tail impact.
- Simulation mode: cluster emulator to run “what-if” scenarios before toggling policy in prod.

Operational experiments & rollout plan
- Phase A: internal-only rollout on canary pool using simulated ledger entries (no billing). Run two-week experiments measuring latency tails and eviction rates.
- Phase B: small cohort of internal customers invited to opt-in to debt model with billing turned on for a small percentage of burst cost (beta pricing).
- Phase C: public opt-in, followed by gradual default enabling for new tenants with conservative debt caps.

Open questions / decisions required:
- How to price amortized cost for heterogeneous model mixes (short-lived large-model bursts vs long-run small-model bursts)?
- Is auto-topup via payment method acceptable as default for standard plans, or must it be opt-in?
- What granularity for ledger retention and how to surface manual adjustments to auditors?

Next steps / action items (owners):
- (Arjun) prototype ledger schema and API (DDEC-PR-01) — due 2025-12-10.
- (Maya) build console mockups for per-tenant burst dashboard and top-up flows — due 2025-12-17.
- (Lars) draft autoscaler integration contract and telemetry spec — due 2026-01-07.
- (Daniela) schedule internal canary and simulation tests, draft runbook — due 2026-01-20.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a sketch: focus review on whether debt semantics and retreat phases are operationally acceptable and if billing alignment is feasible. Look for edge cases where repeated small bursts could build unbounded debt for noisy tenants.

Appendix (quick glossary):
- Credit: unit measuring burst entitlement.
- Debt TTL: time allowed to reconcile negative balance before retreat.
- Fidelity lane: lower-cost/quality model/serving configuration offered to tenants to conserve headroom.
- Retreat: process of gracefully reducing tenant footprint due to unpaid burst debt or pool constraints.
